::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What are good programs for writing expressions?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1098435/what-are-good-programs-for-writing-expressions), asked by [Kelmikra](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/203217/kelmikra) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> By writing expressions, I mean intermediate expressions to "show your work," such as the ones in the below image. LaTex would seem like overkill for such problems.
>
> ![Expressions][q-1]
>
>
>   [q-1]: j0xb2.gif
:::

I still think LaTeX is the way to go.  Once you start having to write several mathematical expressions, any kind of mouse-driven system for specifying them is going to become very frustrating.  LaTeX is extremely efficient for doing exactly what you want to do.

```
\begin{align*}
    c_1x + a     &= c_2 x + b \\
    c_1x + a - a &= c_2x + b - a\\ 
    c_1x         &= c_2x + b - a \\
    c_1x - c_2 x &= c_2x + b - a - c_2 x \\
    c_1x - c_2 x &= b - a \\
    x            &= \frac{b-a}{c_1 - c_2}
\end{align*}
```

$$\begin{align*}
    c_1x + a     &= c_2 x + b \\
    c_1x + a - a &= c_2x + b - a\\ 
    c_1x         &= c_2x + b - a \\
    c_1x - c_2 x &= c_2x + b - a - c_2 x \\
    c_1x - c_2 x &= b - a \\
    x            &= \frac{b-a}{c_1-c_2}
\end{align*}$$

See [Getting started with LaTeX](https://www.tug.org/begin.html) for some pointers.
